title: DirectAdmin Review (2026)
intro: DirectAdmin is evaluated here as a hosting / server control panel for web operations — DirectAdmin is a Linux hosting control panel (JBMC Software) licensed per server — not managed WordPress hosting. Personal Plus publishes at $5/month; Lite $15; Standard $29 with unlimited accounts/domains on published packaging. Same hosting-operations cluster as Plesk and cPanel. Plesk remains the cluster award (7.4); this entity does not outrank it. Landscape-only versus Kinsta/WP Engine managed hosting. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s IT & Development methodology (ease of use, IT job fit, workflow depth, integrations, admin/security, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose DirectAdmin when a low published panel licence is the job — not Plesk by default, and not Kinsta managed hosting.
verdict: Choose DirectAdmin when a low published panel licence is the job — not Plesk by default, and not Kinsta managed hosting. Compare Plesk or cPanel for broader panel ecosystems; Kinsta/WP Engine only on landscape pages for managed hosting. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-18 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, host/GB rates and minimums on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: GUI panel for Linux hosts is approachable; thinner ecosystem UX than Plesk/cPanel. Not a lab test.
Hosting-operations panel licence — ranked with Plesk/cPanel, not managed hosting (Kinsta).
Accounts, domains, and mail cover the panel job; less WordPress/docker toolkit depth than Plesk.
API and hosting-stack hooks; not a SaaS integration graph.
Panel hardening is operator-dependent; adequate for the licence class.
Standard unlimited accounts/domains scales the panel; you still own the metal.
Published $5 Personal Plus floor is the sharpest panel entry here versus Plesk Web Admin. Affiliate economics excluded.
Not an AI product — scored low on the IT methodology’s AI criterion without pretending otherwise.
